hypothesis: Serwist runtimeCaching matches '/api/trips/' with StaleWhileRevalidate (7-day maxAge). When SWR triggers revalidation following a collaborative update, the Service Worker returns the stale cached response, overwriting optimistic UI updates and causing newly added or deleted notes to disappear until browser hard reload.

fetcherWithUserId invokes activeFetch without 'cache: no-store', allowing browser disk cache or intermediate proxies to return cached 200/304 responses during SWR background revalidation, which desynchronizes multi-user collaborative editing states.

broadcastTripEvent dispatches messages on an uncoordinated channel instance without checking SUBSCRIBED status, dropping events during connection phase. Furthermore, receiving tip:update immediately triggers SWR mutate() before the database HTTP PATCH completes, causing the client to fetch uncommitted stale data from Supabase and wipe out live updates.

EditableDailyTips maintains duplicated local state (localNotes, localCosts, localTickets) synchronized via useEffect. When SWR revalidates, stale props overwrite in-flight optimistic user input. Additionally, NoteItem lacks a unique identifier, causing concurrent deletions via array index to delete incorrect items when another collaborator inserts items asynchronously.

EditableDailyChecklist completely lacks Supabase Realtime broadcast support, isolating checklist modifications on a single device. Its internal useState(items) + useEffect([items]) pattern suffers from identical state clashing, where background SWR revalidation overwrites recently checked items.

handleDayDataUpdate modifies SWR state and database but omits saveTripSnapshot, leaving L0 LocalStorage and L1 RAM out of sync. On background wakeup or cold restart, stale snapshots from L0/L1 are reinjected into SWR as fallbackData, resurrecting deleted items or erasing newly added items.
